reasoning: The core problem — locating the best-of-N overoptimization "knee" where proxy reward keeps rising while true task quality plateaus or declines — is directly and fully addressed by published work. Gao et al. (ICML 2023, "Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization") specifically derive the best-of-N functional form (quadratic) showing gold reward peaks then falls as selection pressure increases, and Khalaf et al. (arXiv 2506.19248, 2025) prove the "true reward rises then declines" pattern is an inevitable property of Best-of-N, demonstrated on math/reasoning. "Is Best-of-N the Best of Them?" (arXiv 2503.21878, ICML 2025) further establishes that BoN is non-monotonic in N and provably hacks at large N. The proposal's exact instantiation (best-of-N on GSM8K math with imperfect judge model, watching true accuracy plateau/fall) is even covered by a LessWrong post ("Best-of-n with misaligned reward models for Math reasoning"); the only novelty is using exact-match ground truth instead of a gold reward model, which is a minor methodological variation rather than a new contribution.

evidence.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization (Gao et al., ICML 2023)
evidence.summary: Foundational paper showing that optimizing against a proxy reward model causes gold (true) reward to first rise then fall (Goodhart). Derives the explicit functional form for best-of-N sampling (quadratic in selection pressure) and shows where overoptimization sets in — exactly the BoN 'knee' the proposal seeks to locate.

evidence.title: Inference-Time Reward Hacking in Large Language Models (Khalaf et al., 2025)
evidence.summary: Proves the pattern where true reward first increases then declines is an inevitable property of a broad class of inference-time mechanisms including Best-of-N, demonstrated on math/reasoning and human-preference setups. Directly answers the proposal's question about when selecting harder on a proxy decreases true quality.

evidence.title: Is Best-of-N the Best of Them? Coverage, Scaling, and Optimality in Inference-Time Alignment (ICML 2025)
evidence.summary: Shows best-of-N is not scaling-monotonic: with an inaccurate reward model, regret converges to a non-zero constant and performance degrades as N grows. Characterizes the optimal N (sweet spot) and proves reward hacking at large N — the same overoptimization knee phenomenon.

evidence.title: Best-of-n with misaligned reward models for Math reasoning
evidence.summary: Community study using the proposal's exact setup: best-of-N selection on math reasoning with an imperfect/misaligned reward model, observing true accuracy degrade as selection pressure increases. Demonstrates the cheap, sampling-plus-scoring experimental design the proposal describes has already been carried out.

evidence.title: Better Process Supervision with Bi-directional Rewarding Signals
evidence.summary: Documents the empirical 'scaling decline problem' where post-verification accuracy of outcome/process reward models plateaus or declines as N increases in best-of-N on math benchmarks like GSM8K, attributed to imperfect verifiers misranking candidates — the precise effect the proposal aims to measure.
